newsitem.title: LATVIA: Latvia's Unibanka to enter international markets.
newsitem.headline: Latvia's Unibanka to enter international markets.

text.p: Leading Latvian bank Unibanka plans to enter international capital markets during the first half of the year, Unibanka president Andris Berzinsh said on Monday.
Unibanka plans both to list global depository receipts (GDR) and make a Eurobond issue.
The GDR's would be issued on existing shares of around $10 million before this summer. It would probably involve the state cutting its stake to 10 percent.
"It (the GDR issue) will mainly affect the government's stake," Unibanka president Andris Berzinsh told Reuters in an interview.
The government currently holds 33 percent in Unibanka but is looking to reduce its holding substantially.
"They will remain shareholders but I have information that they intend to keep approximately 10 percent of the total capital," Berzinsh added.
The GDR listing is linked to the bank's plans to do a small eurobond issue by the middle of the year. "I hope to see it in the middle of the year," Berzinsh said.

The bank has been approached by international investment banks interested in managing the offer. Berzinsh said the issue would be small by the Eurobond market standards, where issues normally start from $50 million.
The bank has sufficient capital for its current activities, but Berzinsh said it could need more to expand its operations. He did not rule out another acquisition.
Latvia currently has around 30 banks, although only a few can accept clients' deposits. Berzinsh predicted that within three years, there will be a maximum of four retail banks operating in Latvia.
"Our aim is of course to be one of the leading banks", Berzinsh added.

Unibanka hopes to continue to expand as soon as it has finished the acquistion of fellow commercial bank Zemes Banka. The next step would be taken shortly. He said the bank had concrete plans and ideas.
"Once we understand what we have bought and this acquisition process we have rather ambitious expansion plans," he said.
The merger brings together Unibanka as one of the top banks with Zemes, which is ranked around fifth in the banking market.
Unibanka plans to close most of Zemes Banka's branches down. The move will make around 30 percent of Zemes Banka staff redundant, Berzinsh said.
He said the costs of closures and redundancies would be high but that it was too early to give an estimate of how high they would be.
Zemes currently has 20 branch offices, he said, which compares to Unibanka's 33. Unibanka shareholders are expected to approve the merger with Zemes at a general shareholders meeting on March 25.
Unibanka is one of the leading shares on the Latvian stock exchange and has major Western investors such as the European Bank of Reconstruction and Development (EBRD) and Swedfund.
